Task 6 of 7 in Set up a GenAI prompt · next: Optional: remove the test prompt

Walk it

Steps

Screen
Tools➔Application Extensibility➔Embedded GenAI➔GenAI Prompts (ttrpi5150m000)

Why LN works this way. A change to the prompt text is used by the very next run. A change to the dataset is not seen by a session that is already open. So you can test a text change without reopening the screen, but test a dataset change only after you open the screen again. Each line added here answers something the first answer got wrong or left out.

StepActionYou should see
6.1On GenAI Prompts, tick the prompt, open the arrow beside Edit Text and choose PromptThe text, in the editor
6.2Add a line above the marker that sets the answer's format.
Example

Output plain text only. No heading, no table, no list marks, no bold and no emoji.

6.3Add a line that forbids what the first answer added.
Example

Do not calculate, total or subtract anything, and do not say what can be promised. Report the figures as they are.

6.4Add a line that says how the answer opens.
Example

First line: the item, its description and its inventory unit.

6.5Add a line for one kind of row, with its values in order.
Example

Then one line for each warehouse, written as: warehouse code and name: on hand, blocked, allocated, on order.

6.6Do the same for each other kind of row.
Example

Then the planned inventory transactions, earliest transaction date first, one line each: date, warehouse, order type, order and line, transaction type, planned quantity.

6.7Add the exact words for when there is nothing to report.
Example

If there are no planned inventory transactions, write "Nothing planned in or out."

6.8Add a line for the one thing the reader must not miss.
Example

End with one sentence naming every warehouse whose blocked figure is above zero, with that figure, or saying that none is blocked.

6.9Add a line for a missing value.
Example

If a value you need is not in the dataset, write "[not available]" in its place.

6.10Add a line for how a date is written, then save and close. Example: Write every date as YYYY-MM-DD.A new last-modified stamp
6.11Choose your command again on the same record, without closing the screenThe answer in that form. Example: a line for each warehouse, then a line for each planned receipt and issue
6.12Compare it with your expected values againThe facts should match
6.13Choose your command on a record of each other kind. Example: an item with no stock that customers have ordered, and an item with nothingEach answer fits its record. Example: the two sales orders waiting; the words for nothing planned
6.14Optional: tick a field the answer still lacks in the Modeler, and save. Example: bpid on Planned Inventory Transactions by Item
6.15Optional: add the field to the line of the prompt text that lists its rows' values, then save and close. Example: , business partner at the end of the planned inventory transactions lineA new last-modified stamp
6.16Optional: close the screen's tab, open the record again and choose your commandThe new field is in the answer

If something goes wrong

SymptomWhat to do
The answer includes figures that aren't in LNThe line against calculating may be missing. See step 6.3
The answer is a report or a letter againThe formatting instruction may be missing. See step 6.2
A value reads [not available]The record holds nothing there, the field is not ticked in the dataset, or the screen was open before the dataset was saved. Close its tab and open the record again, as in step 6.16
A type or a status prints as its code, such as act.slsAdd a line that names each code, as in A template for the two texts
A field you ticked is not in the answerThe prompt text may list each line's values without it. Add it to that line, as in step 6.15
The closing sentence names something that does not qualify, or leaves one outCheck it against the screen like any other line. The model can get a comparison wrong, and the next run can differ
The response contradicts the screenThe model reads only the dataset. Read Selected Fields, as in step 2.13 (Model the dataset), then open the screen again

Variations

CaseWhat changes
Keeping the prompt

Stop after this task, and skip the optional last one

Set up a GenAI prompt
Improve it

  1. On GenAI Prompts, tick the prompt, open the arrow beside Edit Text and choose Prompt

    You should see

    The text, in the editor

  2. Add a line above the marker that sets the answer's format.

    Example

    Output plain text only. No heading, no table, no list marks, no bold and no emoji.

  3. Add a line that forbids what the first answer added.

    Example

    Do not calculate, total or subtract anything, and do not say what can be promised. Report the figures as they are.

  4. Add a line that says how the answer opens.

    Example

    First line: the item, its description and its inventory unit.

  5. Add a line for one kind of row, with its values in order.

    Example

    Then one line for each warehouse, written as: warehouse code and name: on hand, blocked, allocated, on order.

  6. Do the same for each other kind of row.

    Example

    Then the planned inventory transactions, earliest transaction date first, one line each: date, warehouse, order type, order and line, transaction type, planned quantity.

  7. Add the exact words for when there is nothing to report.

    Example

    If there are no planned inventory transactions, write "Nothing planned in or out."

  8. Add a line for the one thing the reader must not miss.

    Example

    End with one sentence naming every warehouse whose blocked figure is above zero, with that figure, or saying that none is blocked.

  9. Add a line for a missing value.

    Example

    If a value you need is not in the dataset, write "[not available]" in its place.

  10. Add a line for how a date is written, then save and close

    Example: Write every date as YYYY-MM-DD.

    You should see

    A new last-modified stamp

  11. Choose your command again on the same record, without closing the screen

    You should see

    The answer in that form. Example: a line for each warehouse, then a line for each planned receipt and issue

  12. Compare it with your expected values again

    You should see

    The facts should match

  13. Choose your command on a record of each other kind

    Example: an item with no stock that customers have ordered, and an item with nothing

    You should see

    Each answer fits its record. Example: the two sales orders waiting; the words for nothing planned

  14. Optional: tick a field the answer still lacks in the Modeler, and save

    Example: bpid on Planned Inventory Transactions by Item

  15. Optional: add the field to the line of the prompt text that lists its rows' values, then save and close

    Example: , business partner at the end of the planned inventory transactions line

    You should see

    A new last-modified stamp

  16. Optional: close the screen's tab, open the record again and choose your command

    You should see

    The new field is in the answer

This task starts at Tools➔Application Extensibility➔Embedded GenAI➔GenAI Prompts (ttrpi5150m000)

    • The answer includes figures that aren't in LN

      The line against calculating may be missing. See step 3

    • The answer is a report or a letter again

      The formatting instruction may be missing. See step 2

    • A value reads [not available]

      The record holds nothing there, the field is not ticked in the dataset, or the screen was open before the dataset was saved. Close its tab and open the record again, as in step 16

    • A type or a status prints as its code, such as act.sls

      Add a line that names each code, as in A template for the two texts

    • A field you ticked is not in the answer

      The prompt text may list each line's values without it. Add it to that line, as in step 15

    • The closing sentence names something that does not qualify, or leaves one out

      Check it against the screen like any other line. The model can get a comparison wrong, and the next run can differ

    • The response contradicts the screen

      The model reads only the dataset. Read Selected Fields, as in step 13 of Model the dataset, then open the screen again

  • A change to the prompt text is used by the very next run. A change to the dataset is not seen by a session that is already open. So you can test a text change without reopening the screen, but test a dataset change only after you open the screen again. Each line added here answers something the first answer got wrong or left out.
